drills.q: Name what transformers, datasets, and accelerate each own in the HF stack.
drills.a: transformers: uniform model/tokenizer interface. datasets: Arrow-backed memory-mapped/streamable data loading. accelerate: topology-agnostic training launch and mixed precision, used internally even in single-GPU trl training.

drills.q: You download a .bin checkpoint from an unfamiliar Hub repo. What's the risk and what should you do instead?
drills.a: Pickle-based .bin can execute arbitrary code on load via __reduce__. Prefer a safetensors version of the same model if available, and never load an untrusted pickle checkpoint.

drills.q: A colleague proposes deploying a new production LLM service on TGI in 2026. What do you tell them?
drills.a: TGI entered maintenance mode in December 2025; HF itself recommends vLLM or SGLang for new production serving. Building new infrastructure on a maintenance-mode dependency accumulates avoidable migration risk.

drills.q: Compute the trainable-parameter reduction from LoRA on a 4096x4096 weight matrix with rank r=16.
drills.a: Full: 4096×4096 ≈ 16.8M params. LoRA: r(d+k) = 16×(4096+4096) = 131,072 params — roughly 128x fewer trainable parameters for that matrix.

drills.q: You need to fine-tune a 70B model on a single 80GB GPU. What combination of techniques makes this feasible, and why?
drills.a: QLoRA: load the frozen base in 4-bit NF4 quantization (with double quantization) to shrink its memory footprint roughly 4x, then train LoRA adapters in bf16 on top — full-precision fine-tuning of the whole model would require multiple 80GB GPUs.

drills.q: Your model's production behavior changes overnight with no deploy on your team's side, loaded via from_pretrained without a revision argument. Diagnose and fix.
drills.a: Loading from an unpinned 'main' branch means the repo owner's latest push is what gets loaded on the next cold start/cache miss. Fix: pin an explicit commit hash via revision="<hash>" in every production from_pretrained call.

drills.q: A data pipeline using datasets in streaming mode can't reproduce a proper global shuffle across epochs. Why, and what are the options?
drills.a: Streaming mode has no random access, only iteration with buffer-based approximate shuffling. Options: accept approximate shuffling with a large buffer, pre-shard and shuffle shard order per epoch, or switch to non-streaming (memory-mapped) mode if local disk can hold the data.

drills.q: A CTO wants to rewrite an existing working LangChain-based product entirely off LangChain after reading a blog post. How do you respond?
drills.a: Audit what's actually being used first — LangGraph-based durable agent state is a different, often still-justified case from simple LCEL chains that could be a few lines of plain Python. A full rewrite trades a real, bounded rewrite/regression risk for a benefit that may only apply to part of the codebase.

drills.q: Explain why nobody actually swapping vector databases in production undermines one common argument for using LangChain's retriever wrapper layer.
drills.a: The wrapper's main pitch is portability across vector stores, but since teams rarely swap vector DBs once committed, the portability benefit is rarely exercised while the abstraction still costs a layer of indirection over the native client's fuller control (custom filtering, hybrid search tuning).

drills.q: You need to post-train a model on a task with a cheap, automatically verifiable correctness check (e.g. unit tests passing). Would you reach for DPO or GRPO, and why?
drills.a: GRPO — it exploits verifiable reward signals directly via group-relative advantage estimation from sampled completions, whereas DPO requires collecting preference pairs, which is unnecessary overhead when a cheap verifier already exists.

drills.q: Training loss looks good but held-out eval is worse than the base model after a LoRA fine-tune. What are your first two hypotheses?
drills.a: 1) Catastrophic forgetting from too-aggressive a learning rate or too many epochs on a narrow dataset relative to LoRA rank. 2) The adapter isn't actually being loaded at eval time (get_peft_model wrapping omitted), silently evaluating the frozen base instead.
